documents.title: Book Closure For The Purpose Of 34Th AGM
Addendum To The Boards'' Report For The Financial Year 2025-26 Which Forms An Integral Part Of The 34Th Annual Report

analysis.summary: Kernex Microsystems (India) Limited reported robust financial performance for Q1 FY2026-27, with significant order execution and revenue growth. The company highlights its market position in railway safety systems, particularly Kavach 4.0, along with expanding manufacturing capacities and working capital limits. Management also outlined a strategic diversification roadmap into various technology and infrastructure domains to reduce single-vertical dependency. Kernex Microsystems (India) Ltd reported its Q3 FY25 and 9M FY25 financial performance, showcasing significant growth in revenue, EBITDA, and profit after tax compared to the previous year. Management outlined ongoing TCAS projects, production capacities, order book details, and timelines for upcoming railway safety and signalling initiatives.

demand_outlook.claim: The company notes that Indian Railways adds approximately 5 new locomotives daily, which continuously grows the national rolling stock asset base.
demand_outlook.quote: Expanding Fleet Baseline: Indian Railways adds ~approx 5 new locomotives daily (~1,900+ per annum), continuously growing the national rolling stock asset base.

demand_outlook.claim: Management stated that the Railway's Pink book has planned an execution of ~Rs 35,000 Crores Opportunity for Kavach for next 5 yrs.
demand_outlook.quote: Railway’sPinkbookhasalready plannedanexecutionof ~Rs 35,000 Crores Opportunity Kavachfornext5 yrs

capex_expansion.claim: The company is expanding manufacturing capacity ahead of order inflow and mobilising resources in advance.
capex_expansion.quote: Capacity build-out ahead of demand: The Company is expanding capacity in advance of order inflow. Recruitment of technical and project personnel is under way on a forward-looking basis, and engineering, installation and commissioning resources are being mobilised ahead of anticipated awards, so that execution capability is established before contracts are received.

orders_capacity.claim: The total orders received stand at 5,174 Crores with 1,687 Crores executed by KMIL, leaving a balance order book of 3,487 Crores.
orders_capacity.quote: Total Orders Received Executed by KMIL Balance Order Book ₹5,174 Cr − ₹1,687 Cr =− ₹3,487 Cr 33% of total value delivered 67% remaining to execute
